claim: The Notch-Delta pathway is required to distinguish target from non-target muscles in C. elegans egg-laying circuit.
source_text: We found that the Notch-Delta pathway was required to distinguish target from non-target muscles.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data from genetic screens and mutant analysis showing that mutations in Notch-Delta pathway components affect muscle target selection.

claim: APX-1/Delta acts in surrounding cells including the non-target vm1 to activate LIN-12/Notch in the target vm2.
source_text: APX-1/Delta acts in surrounding cells including the non-target vm1 to activate LIN-12/Notch in the target vm2.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by expression pattern analysis and cell-specific rescue experiments demonstrating where APX-1 is expressed and where it functions.

claim: LIN-12 functions cell-autonomously to up-regulate the expression of UNC-40/DCC and MADD-2 in vm2.
source_text: LIN-12 functions cell-autonomously to up-regulate the expression of UNC-40/DCC and MADD-2 in vm2, which in turn function together to promote muscle arm formation and guidance.
evidence_reasoning: Supported by mosaic analysis, cell-specific rescue experiments, and expression pattern analysis showing LIN-12 regulates UNC-40 and MADD-2 expression in vm2 cells.

claim: Ectopic expression of UNC-40/DCC in non-target vm1 muscle is sufficient to induce muscle arm extension from these cells.
source_text: Ectopic expression of UNC-40/DCC in non-target vm1 muscle is sufficient to induce muscle arm extension from these cells.
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through transgenic experiments where UNC-40 was expressed in vm1 cells and resulted in ectopic muscle arm-like structures.

claim: The LIN-12/Notch signaling specifies target selection by selectively up-regulating guidance molecules and forming muscle arms in target cells.
source_text: Therefore, the LIN-12/Notch signaling specifies target selection by selectively up-regulating guidance molecules and forming muscle arms in target cells.
evidence_reasoning: This is a summary conclusion drawn from multiple experimental observations including expression patterns, mutant phenotypes, and rescue experiments.

claim: Presynaptic neurons HSN and VC4/5 form synapses exclusively on vm2 muscle cells in C. elegans.
source_text: While vm1 and vm2 are from a common lineage, are physically adjacent and share many molecular components, the egg-laying motoneurons HSN and VC4/5 form serotoninergic and cholinergic chemical synapses exclusively on vm2
evidence_reasoning: Supported by cited EM reconstruction studies and confirmed by the authors' fluorescence imaging data.

claim: HSN presynaptic specializations are closely juxtaposed against dendritic spine-like membrane protrusions (muscle arms) from vm2 cell bodies.
source_text: Consistent with EM reconstruction, we found that the HSN presynaptic specializations were closely juxtaposed against the dendritic spine-like membrane protrusions (muscle arms) from the vm2 cell bodies when viewed from both the lateral and ventral sides
evidence_reasoning: Confirmed by the authors' fluorescence imaging and consistent with previously published EM reconstruction data.

claim: UNC-103E is dramatically enriched on vm2 muscle arms.
source_text: low level of transgenic expression of UNC-103E::GFP with an integrated single-copy transgene showed that UNC-103E was dramatically enriched on vm2 muscle arms
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through fluorescence imaging of single-copy transgenic animals expressing UNC-103E::GFP.

claim: HSN neurons are not required for vm2 specification and muscle arm development.
source_text: We therefore asked whether the HSN neurons are required for vm2 specification and muscle arm development by examining the vm2 morphology in the egl-1(n986) mutant, in which the HSN neurons undergo programmed cell death in embryonic stage. Surprisingly, in all of the examined animals, the morphology and position of vm2 muscle arms were indistinguishable from the wild type counterparts
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through analysis of egl-1 mutants lacking HSN neurons, which still develop normal vm2 muscle arms.

claim: Vulval epithelial cells are required for normal vulval muscle differentiation and morphogenesis.
source_text: We examined the vm2 muscle arm morphology in lin-3(e1417) mutant animals, in which vulval epithelial cell fate is abnormal, and observed severe defects on both vulval muscle morphology and muscle arm development. This result suggests that the vulval epithelial cells are required for normal vulval muscle differentiation and morphogenesis
evidence_reasoning: Based on observed phenotypes in lin-3 mutants where vulval epithelial cell fate is disrupted.

claim: lin-12(wy750) is a partial loss-of-function allele containing a single missense mutation (G473R) in one of the conserved extracellular EGF domains.
source_text: Sequence analyses revealed that lin-12(wy750) contained a single missense mutation (G473R) in one of the conserved extracellular EGF domains of the LIN-12 protein.
evidence_reasoning: Determined through DNA sequencing of the mutant allele.

claim: lin-12(wy750) mutants have normal vulval morphogenesis but defective vm2 muscle arm development.
source_text: In lin-12(wy750) mutant animals, while the muscle morphology of both vm1 and vm2 were largely normal, the SER-1B::GFP labeled vm2 muscle arm structures were completely absent
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through fluorescence microscopy and DIC imaging of lin-12(wy750) mutants.

claim: Muscle arm defective mutants lay notably fewer eggs compared to wild-type animals.
source_text: First, the muscle arm defective mutants laid notably fewer eggs compared to the wild-type animals
evidence_reasoning: Quantified through egg-laying assays comparing wild-type and mutant animals.

claim: lin-12(wy750) and apx-1(wy755) mutants have asynchronous vulval muscle Ca2+ transients leading to uncoordinated contractions.
source_text: However, double Ca2+ transients were often asynchronous, with significant delays between anterior and posterior vulval muscle transients that resulted in uncoordinated vulval muscle contractions that were not able to release eggs
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through ratiometric Ca2+ imaging in behaving animals.

claim: lin-12(wy750) and apx-1(wy755) mutants had a twofold increase in the frequency of Ca2+ transient peaks compared to wild type.
source_text: As a result, lin-12(wy750) and apx-1(wy755) mutants had a twofold increase in the frequency of Ca2+ transient peaks
evidence_reasoning: Quantified from Ca2+ imaging recordings and statistical analysis.

claim: The average anterior/posterior delay in double Ca2+ transients increased from ~100 ms in wild type to ~800 ms in lin-12(wy750) and apx-1(wy755) mutants.
source_text: In wild-type animals, the average anterior/posterior delay was only ∼100 ms, as nearly all double transients were not resolved into separate anterior/posterior peaks at the temporal and spatial resolution of our ΔR/R traces. In both lin-12(wy750) and apx-1(wy755) mutants, the average anterior/posterior delay in double Ca2+ transients increased to ∼800 ms
evidence_reasoning: Measured from Ca2+ imaging data with temporal resolution analysis.

claim: vm2 muscle arms are required for synchronous excitation of anterior and posterior vulval muscles needed to successfully execute egg-laying behavior.
source_text: Together, these results show that the vm2 muscle arms lacking in lin-12(wy750) and apx-1(wy755) mutants are not necessary for excitation of the vulval muscles, but suggest they are required for the synchronous excitation of anterior and posterior vulval muscles needed to successfully execute egg-laying behavior.
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from Ca2+ imaging and behavioral observations showing asynchronous activation in mutants lacking muscle arms.

claim: Muscle arm development requires a higher level of LIN-12/Notch signaling activity compared with vulval morphogenesis.
source_text: These data suggest that partial loss of LIN-12/Notch signaling activity spares vulval morphogenesis but specifically impairs vm2 specification and muscle arm development, and that muscle arm development might require a higher level of LIN-12/Notch signaling activity compared with earlier developmental events
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from the observation that weak alleles affect muscle arms but not vulval morphogenesis, while strong alleles affect both.

claim: LIN-12/Notch signaling functions at the L4 stage to specify vm2 postsynaptic identity and muscle arm development.
source_text: The upshift and downshift experiments together suggest a novel function of lin-12 at the L4 stage in regulating the postsynaptic muscle arm development and synaptic target choice.
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through temperature shift experiments using temperature-sensitive alleles.

claim: LIN-12/Notch signaling functions cell-autonomously in vm2 to regulate postsynaptic specification and muscle arm development.
source_text: We next investigated where lin-12 was required. We performed mosaic analysis using a lin-12 genomic fragment fused with SL2::mCherry. We found that the expression of lin-12 in vm2 was sufficient to rescue the muscle arm defects in lin-12(wy750) mutants
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through mosaic analysis and cell-specific rescue experiments.

claim: APX-1 is expressed in secondary vulval epithelial cells and vm1 cells.
source_text: We found that apx-1 was expressed in the secondary vulval epithelial cells and vm1 cells
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through expression pattern analysis using fluorescent reporters.

claim: APX-1 functions non-cell-autonomously to activate LIN-12/Notch signaling in vm2.
source_text: Interestingly, the expression of apx-1 in either the secondary vulval epithelial cells or vm1 cells was sufficient to rescue the muscle arm defects in apx-1(wy755) mutants, indicating that apx-1 functions non-cell-autonomously
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through cell-specific rescue experiments showing APX-1 acts from neighboring cells.

claim: SEL-12 functions cell-autonomously in vm2 to regulate muscle arm development.
source_text: We found that expression of sel-12 in vulval muscle cells completely rescued the vm2 muscle arm phenotype of sel-12(wy760), consistent with the cell-autonomous requirement of LIN-12/Notch signaling in vm2
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through cell-specific rescue experiments.

claim: The canonical LIN-12/Notch pathway controls transcription of downstream genes involved in muscle arm development.
source_text: Additionally, specific expression of a dominant-negative lag-1 construct in the vulval muscles phenocopied the muscle arm defects observed in lin-12(wy750), apx-1(wy750) and sel-12(wy760) mutants, suggesting that the canonical LIN-12/Notch pathway is likely involved by controlling the transcription of downstream genes.
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through dominant-negative experiments targeting the transcriptional component of the pathway.

claim: hlh-29 is a target gene of the canonical LIN-12/Notch pathway in vm2.
source_text: Moreover, the expression of a hlh-29 transcription reporter (hlh-29::gfp), a known target gene of the canonical LIN-12/Notch pathway in vm2, was also dramatically down-regulated in lin-12(wy750), apx-1(wy755) and sel-12(wy760) mutants
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through reporter expression analysis and supported by previous literature identifying hlh-29 as a Notch target.

claim: apx-1 unilaterally promotes lin-12 expression and activates the LIN-12/Notch pathway in vm2.
source_text: Compared with wild-type animals, apx-1(wy755) mutant animals showed significantly reduced expression of lin-12 in vm2 cells, whereas the lin-12 expression in vulval epithelial cells was not affected. On the other hand, we did not observe any change of apx-1 expression in the lin-12(wy750) mutant. These results argue that apx-1 unilaterally promotes lin-12 expression and activates the LIN-12/Notch pathway in vm2.
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from expression pattern analysis showing asymmetric regulation between apx-1 and lin-12.

claim: The lin-12 promoter contains three LAG-1 consensus binding sites.
source_text: Indeed, we found three LAG-1 consensus binding sites in the promoter region of lin-12
evidence_reasoning: Identified through sequence analysis of the lin-12 promoter region.

claim: Muscle arm development requires the positive transcriptional feedback of the LIN-12/Notch pathway.
source_text: We sequenced the lin-12 promoter in this allele and found a 541-bp deletion in the promoter region leading to the deletion of two of the three LAG-1 binding sites. Interestingly, the muscle arm development was similarly affected in lin-12(e2621), suggesting that the muscle arm development might require the positive transcriptional feedback of the LIN-12/Notch pathway.
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from the phenotype of a promoter deletion mutant that removes LAG-1 binding sites.

claim: UNC-40/DCC is a homolog of Deleted in Colorectal Carcinoma (DCC) and neogenin in vertebrates.
source_text: UNC-40, which is a homolog of Deleted in Colorectal Carcinoma (DCC) and neogenin in vertebrates serving as a receptor for the UNC-6/Netrin ligand
evidence_reasoning: Based on established knowledge of protein homology and cited literature.

claim: UNC-40 plays critical roles in the formation of dendritic spine-like postsynaptic muscle arms of body wall muscles in worms.
source_text: In addition, UNC-40 plays critical roles in the formation of dendritic spine-like postsynaptic muscle arms of the body wall muscles in worms
evidence_reasoning: Supported by cited previous studies on UNC-40 function.

claim: unc-40 and madd-2 loss-of-function mutants show vm2 muscle arm defects.
source_text: Indeed, we found that unc-40 and madd-2 loss-of-function mutants showed vm2 muscle arm defects, similar to the phenotype found in the lin-12(wy750) mutants.
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through phenotypic analysis of mutant animals.

claim: Both UNC-40 and MADD-2 are preferentially expressed in vm2 cells.
source_text: In wild-type animals, both UNC-40 and MADD-2 translational reporters were preferentially expressed in vm2 cells
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through fluorescent reporter expression analysis.

claim: The expression of both UNC-40 and MADD-2 in vm2 is significantly down-regulated in the lin-12(wy750) mutant.
source_text: The expression of both UNC-40 and MADD-2 in vm2 was significantly down-regulated in the lin-12(wy750) mutant, supporting the idea that lin-12 was required for the expression of unc-40 and madd-2 in vm2.
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through comparison of reporter expression in wild-type and mutant animals.

claim: The canonical LIN-12/Notch signaling pathway acts to promote the transcriptions of both unc-40 and madd-2.
source_text: Both unc-40 and madd-2 were preferentially transcribed in vm2 cells, and the transcriptional activities of both promoters were dramatically suppressed in the lin-12(wy750) mutant. These data indicate that the canonical LIN-12/Notch signaling pathway acts to promote the transcriptions of both unc-40 and madd-2 directly.
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through transcriptional reporter analysis and inferred from the presence of LAG-1 binding sites.

claim: Two LAG-1 consensus binding sites are found on the proximal promoter region of the madd-2 gene.
source_text: Consistent with this model, two LAG-1 consensus binding sites were found on the proximal promoter region of the madd-2 gene.
evidence_reasoning: Identified through sequence analysis of the madd-2 promoter.

claim: Two LAG-1 binding sites are found in the third intron of unc-40.
source_text: Although no LAG-1 binding site was found in unc-40 promoter region, two were found in the third intron of unc-40 that is essential for its expression
evidence_reasoning: Identified through sequence analysis and supported by personal communication regarding the importance of this intron.

claim: Forced expression of UNC-40 in vm2 from the unc-103e promoter induces the formation of muscle arms in the lin-12(wy750) mutant.
source_text: We found that the forced expression of UNC-40 in vm2 from the unc-103e promoter induced the formation of muscle arms in the lin-12(wy750) mutant
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through transgenic rescue experiments.

claim: Misexpression of UNC-40 is sufficient to induce dendritic spine-like membrane extensions from vm1 cells.
source_text: We found that misexpression of UNC-40 was sufficient to induce the dendritic spine-like membrane extensions from vm1 cells
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through ectopic expression experiments in vm1 cells.

claim: UNC-40 responds to specific environmental cues to guide the formation of muscle arms.
source_text: Although the ectopic membrane extension from vm1 was usually thinner than the wild-type vm2 muscle arm, the vm1 muscle arms always formed from the medial surface of vm1, the identical location as for the normal vm2 muscle arms, suggesting that UNC-40 responds to specific environmental cues to guide the formation of muscle arms.
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from the stereotyped location of ectopic muscle arms induced by UNC-40 expression.

claim: unc-40 and madd-2 function at least partly in parallel pathways.
source_text: We generated an unc-40(n324); madd-2(ok2226) double mutant and found slightly enhanced muscle arm defects in the double mutants... Expression of madd-2 and unc-40 is not mutually regulated, consistent to the hypothesis that unc-40 and madd-2 at least partly function in parallel.
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from genetic interaction analysis and expression pattern studies.

claim: Overexpression of unc-40 largely rescued the muscle arm defects of madd-2(ok2226) mutant.
source_text: Conversely, overexpression of unc-40 largely rescued the muscle arm defects of madd-2(ok2226) mutant, suggesting that madd-2 likely functioned synergistically with unc-40 to promote muscle arm formation
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through overexpression rescue experiments.

claim: madd-2 potentiates the activity of unc-40 in muscle arm development.
source_text: In both the Netrin-mediated axon attracting process and Netrin-independent body wall muscle arm extension process, madd-2 potentiates the activity of unc-40
evidence_reasoning: Supported by cited literature and confirmed by the authors' genetic interaction studies.

claim: unc-40 plays a deterministic role in guiding the muscle arm extension and the postsynaptic target selection.
source_text: Taken together, these results demonstrate that unc-40, potentiated by madd-2, plays a deterministic role in guiding the muscle arm extension and the postsynaptic target selection.
evidence_reasoning: Concluded from multiple lines of evidence including rescue experiments, ectopic expression, and genetic interactions.

claim: The formation of pre- and postsynaptic specializations can occur at different times in the egg-laying circuit.
source_text: First, the formation of pre- and postsynaptic specializations can occur at different times. The HSN presynaptic specializations form at the early L4 stage, significantly before the maturation of the postsynaptic targets. The extension of the postsynaptic muscle arms takes place 5–6 hr later.
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through developmental time course observations.

claim: The development of the pre- and postsynaptic specializations appears to be independent of each other.
source_text: Second, the development of the pre- and postsynaptic specializations appears to be independent of each other. Eliminating the postsynaptic cells does not affect the timing and location of synaptic vesicle accumulation in HSN neurons. Similarly, ablation of the presynaptic neurons has no obvious effect on the timing and direction of the muscle arm growth
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through cell ablation experiments and cited previous work.

claim: Primary vulval epithelial cells serve as guidepost cells for HSN presynaptic development.
source_text: Through genetic analysis, we previously found that the primary vulval epithelial cells serve as guidepost cells for the HSN presynaptic development
evidence_reasoning: Based on the authors' previously published work.

claim: Postsynaptic differentiation is likely guided by the secondary vulval epithelial cells.
source_text: Interestingly, postsynaptic differentiation is likely guided by the secondary vulval epithelial cells
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from expression patterns and rescue experiments showing APX-1 function in secondary cells.

claim: The muscle arms grow along the interface between the primary and the secondary vulval epithelial cells.
source_text: The muscle arms appear to grow along the interface between the primary and the secondary vulval epithelial cells through possibly an UNC-40-dependent mechanism
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from anatomical observations and the role of UNC-40 in muscle arm guidance.

claim: The epithelial cells play organizational roles for the development of the entire vulval organ.
source_text: The epithelial cells not only function as the channel for egg-laying but also play organizational roles for the development of the entire vulval organ, coordinating multiple events including vulval muscle migration, axon guidance of HSN, VC axon branching and synapse formation.
evidence_reasoning: Concluded from the multiple developmental processes shown to depend on epithelial cells.

claim: LIN-12/Notch signaling instructs both vulval organogenesis and synaptic development of the egg-laying circuit by regulating at least three sequential but independent developmental processes.
source_text: Therefore, we conclude that LIN-12/Notch signal instructs both vulval organogenesis and synaptic development of the egg-laying circuit by regulating at least three sequential but independent developmental processes: the AC/VU decision, in which LIN-12/Notch signaling promotes the differentiation of AC and VU cells; VPC specification, in which it determines the vulval precursor cell fates; and vm2 postsynaptic specification, in which it specifies the postsynaptic target cell and further regulates the muscle arm development.
evidence_reasoning: Synthesized conclusion from the authors' data combined with established knowledge of LIN-12 function in earlier developmental processes.

claim: vm1 is mainly controlled by vm2 via gap junctions.
source_text: vm1 is mainly controlled by vm2 via gap junctions
evidence_reasoning: Based on cited EM reconstruction studies.

claim: vm2 receives some additional synapses with the ventral nerve cord besides HSN and VC4/5.
source_text: Besides forming major synaptic connection on HSN and VC4/5, vm2 also receive some additional synapses with the ventral nerve cord
evidence_reasoning: Based on personal communication cited in the manuscript.

claim: HSN axon guidance and presynaptic formation preceded both axon growth of VC neurons and vulval muscle differentiation.
source_text: Developmental studies showed that HSN axon guidance and presynaptic formation preceded both axon growth of VC neurons and vulval muscle differentiation
evidence_reasoning: Based on the authors' developmental time course observations.

claim: In egl-1(n986);lin-39(n709) double mutant animals which lacked both HSN and VC neurons, the vm2 muscle arms still existed.
source_text: First, in a portion of the egl-1(n986);lin-39(n709) double mutant animals which lacked both HSN and VC neurons, the vm2 muscle arms still existed
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through analysis of double mutant animals.

claim: In unc-104(e1265) mutant animals, in which the synaptic vesicles were absent from the presynaptic regions in both HSN and VC neurons, vm2 muscle arm development was not affected.
source_text: Second, in unc-104(e1265) mutant animals, in which the synaptic vesicles were absent from the presynaptic regions in both HSN and VC neurons, vm2 muscle arm development was not affected
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through analysis of unc-104 mutants.

claim: Presynaptic components are dispensable for vm2 postsynaptic development.
source_text: These results indicate that presynaptic components are dispensable for vm2 postsynaptic development.
evidence_reasoning: Concluded from experiments showing normal muscle arm development in the absence of presynaptic neurons or vesicles.

claim: lin-12(wy750) mutants show no vulval morphogenesis defect.
source_text: Surprisingly, we found no vulval morphogenesis defect in lin-12(wy750) mutants either by differential interference contrast (DIC) microscopy or the localization pattern of the ajm-1::gfp apical junction marker at several development stages
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through DIC microscopy and fluorescent marker analysis.

claim: Both HSN and VC presynaptic markers appeared normal in the lin-12(wy750) mutant.
source_text: Both HSN and VC presynaptic markers appeared normal in the lin-12(wy750) mutant, indicating that the mutation specifically affected postsynaptic differentiation and development
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through fluorescent marker analysis of presynaptic proteins.

claim: The muscle arm defects in vm2 in lin-12(wy750) mutants are not due to a change of vm2 cell fate to a different cell.
source_text: We considered the possibility that the absence of muscle arms in vm2 could be due to the change of vm2 cell fate to a different cell. We therefore examined several cell-type-specific markers for each differentiation stage... In lin-12(wy750) mutants, all three markers exhibits wild type pattern, suggesting that many molecular signatures of the M lineage are intact in the lin-12(wy750) mutants
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through analysis of multiple cell-type-specific markers showing normal patterns.

claim: No significant difference was found on the intersection angle between the vulval muscle and the vulval slit in lin-12(wy750) mutants compared to wild type.
source_text: No significant difference was found on the intersection angle between the vulval muscle and the vulval slit, as well as the relative size of vm2 to vm1 (Svm2/Svm1)
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through quantitative morphological analysis.

claim: Mutants with defective vm2 muscle arm development show altered egg-laying behavior.
source_text: If vm2 muscle arms play crucial functional roles in the synaptic connections of the egg-laying circuit, mutants with defective vm2 muscle arm development should show altered egg-laying behavior.
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through egg-laying assays and Ca2+ imaging experiments.

claim: Muscle arm defective mutants laid significantly more late-stage embryos compared to wild-type animals.
source_text: Second, the muscle arm defective mutants laid significantly more late-stage embryos compared to the wild-type animals
evidence_reasoning: Quantified through egg-laying assays examining embryo developmental stages.

claim: In wild-type animals, simultaneous Ca2+ transients in the anterior and posterior vulval muscles drive synchronous muscle contraction and release of eggs.
source_text: In wild-type animals, simultaneous Ca2+ transients in the anterior and posterior vulval muscles, which we call 'double' transients, drive synchronous muscle contraction and release of eggs
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through Ca2+ imaging and supported by cited previous work.

claim: lin-12(wy750) and apx-1(wy755) vm2 muscle arm mutants were still able to execute single anterior and posterior vulval muscle Ca2+ transients.
source_text: Despite their lack of postsynaptic muscle arms, we found that lin-12(wy750) and apx-1(wy755) vm2 muscle arm mutants were still able to execute single anterior and posterior vulval muscle Ca2+ transients, which was presumably due to the intact minor synaptic inputs from the ventral nerve cord alongside the vulval muscles
evidence_reasoning: Observed through Ca2+ imaging and inferred based on known anatomical connections.

claim: lin-12(wy750) and apx-1(wy755) mutants had significantly fewer synchronous double transients compared to the wild type.
source_text: We also found that lin-12(wy750) and apx-1(wy755) mutants had significantly fewer synchronous double transients compared to the wild type
evidence_reasoning: Quantified from Ca2+ imaging recordings.

claim: The egg-laying defect in lin-12(wy750) and apx-1(wy755) mutants is not caused by structural problems in the vulva itself.
source_text: In the rare instances when strong single transients or asynchronously initiated anterior/posterior Ca2+ transients of lin-12(wy750) and apx-1(wy755) mutants led to opening of the vulva, egg-laying would still occur, indicating that their egg-laying defect was not caused by structural problems in the vulva itself
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from observations of successful egg-laying events in mutants when sufficient vulval opening occurred.

claim: trans-heterozygotes between lin-12(wy750) and a canonical loss-of-function allele lin-12(n676n930) presented similar muscle arm defects.
source_text: First, trans-heterozygotes between lin-12(wy750) and a canonical loss-of-function allele lin-12(n676n930) presented similar muscle arm defects
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through genetic complementation analysis.

claim: A lin-12 genomic fragment including 5 kb of upstream regulatory sequence and the entire coding region of lin-12 strongly rescued the muscle arm phenotype of lin-12(wy750) mutants.
source_text: Second, a lin-12 genomic fragment including 5 kb of upstream regulatory sequence and the entire coding region of lin-12 strongly rescued the muscle arm phenotype of lin-12(wy750) mutants
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through transgenic rescue experiments.

claim: Strong loss-of-function alleles of lin-12, apx-1 and sel-12 cause lethality, dramatic vulval morphogenesis or general muscle morphology phenotypes.
source_text: Since strong loss-of-function alleles of lin-12, apx-1 and sel-12 cause lethality, dramatic vulval morphogenesis or general muscle morphology phenotypes, which are all absent in lin-12(wy750) mutant animals, it is likely that the missense mutation we isolated represents a partial loss-of-function allele.
evidence_reasoning: Based on established knowledge from previous literature about strong loss-of-function alleles.

claim: One early-stop mutation in the sel-12 coding region leads to additional pleiotropic effects on both vulval muscle patterning and vulval morphogenesis.
source_text: One early-stop mutation in the sel-12 coding region leads to additional pleiotropic effects on both vulval muscle patterning and vulval morphogenesis, while the other missense mutation of sel-12 causes specific muscle arm defect
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through phenotypic analysis of different sel-12 alleles.

claim: Partial loss of LIN-12/Notch signaling activity spares vulval morphogenesis but specifically impairs vm2 specification and muscle arm development.
source_text: Together, these data suggest that partial loss of LIN-12/Notch signaling activity spares vulval morphogenesis but specifically impairs vm2 specification and muscle arm development
evidence_reasoning: Inferred from the differential effects of weak vs strong alleles on different developmental processes.

claim: More than 80% of lin-12(n676n930) animals shifted from 25°C to 15°C at mid-L4 still showed defective muscle arms.
source_text: More than 80% of the animals still showed defective muscle arms when shifted from 25°C to 15°C at mid-L4
evidence_reasoning: Quantified from temperature shift experiments.

claim: lin-12 function in regulating postsynaptic muscle arm development is independent of other known roles of lin-12, all of which occur prior to early-L4 stage.
source_text: The upshift and downshift experiments together suggest a novel function of lin-12 at the L4 stage in regulating the postsynaptic muscle arm development and synaptic target choice. This lin-12 function is independent of other known roles of lin-12, all of which occur prior to early-L4 stage.
evidence_reasoning: Concluded from temperature shift experiments showing late requirement for lin-12 function.

claim: The expression of lin-12 in vm2 was sufficient to rescue the muscle arm defects in lin-12(wy750) mutants.
source_text: We found that the expression of lin-12 in vm2 was sufficient to rescue the muscle arm defects in lin-12(wy750) mutants
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through mosaic analysis experiments.

claim: apx-1 is expressed in the secondary vulval epithelial cells and vm1 cells but not in vm2 cells.
source_text: We found that apx-1 was expressed in the secondary vulval epithelial cells and vm1 cells
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through expression pattern analysis using fluorescent reporters.

claim: The expression of apx-1 in either the secondary vulval epithelial cells or vm1 cells was sufficient to rescue the muscle arm defects in apx-1(wy755) mutants.
source_text: Interestingly, the expression of apx-1 in either the secondary vulval epithelial cells or vm1 cells was sufficient to rescue the muscle arm defects in apx-1(wy755) mutants
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through cell-specific rescue experiments.

claim: The vm2 muscle arms are located between the primary and secondary vulval epithelial cells and directly contact these cells.
source_text: We found that the vm2 muscle arms were located between the primary and secondary vulval epithelial cells and directly contact these cells
evidence_reasoning: Demonstrated through confocal microscopy analysis of cell positions.

claim: apx-1(wy755); lin-12(wy750) double mutants showed similar muscle arm defects as single mutants.
source_text: Based on the cell-autonomous function of lin-12 and the non-cell-autonomous function of apx-1, we predicted that apx-1(wy755); lin-12(wy750) double mutants should show similar muscle arm defects as single mutants. Indeed, we found that the double mutants showed similar muscle arm defects as single mutants
evidence_reasoning: Predicted based on genetic logic and confirmed through analysis of double mutants.

claim: UNC-40::GFP showed membrane-associated pattern and was enriched on vm2 muscle arms.
source_text: UNC-40::GFP showed membrane-associated pattern and was enriched on vm2 muscle arms.
evidence_reasoning: Observed through fluorescence microscopy of translational reporter.

claim: MADD-2 was distributed diffusely in vm2 cells.
source_text: MADD-2 was distributed diffusely in vm2 cells.
